cards.title: Classes pick some elements
cards.body: Give elements a `class`, then style that class with a dot, like `.note`. Only elements with the class change.
cards.code:
A plain paragraph.

A paragraph with a class.

hi.title: Classes kuch elements chunti hain
hi.body: Elements ko ek `class` do, phir us class ko dot ke saath style karo, jaise `.note`. Sirf us class wale elements badlenge.

cards.title: One class, many elements
cards.body: Many elements can share a class, so one rule styles all of them at once.

hi.title: Ek class, kai elements
hi.body: Kai elements ek hi class share kar sakte hain, isliye ek rule sabko ek saath style kar deta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: The paragraph should be light blue, but nothing changes. Which line is wrong?
cards.code: Remember the milk.

bug.fix: A class rule starts with a dot: `.note`. Without it, CSS looks for a `<note>` tag, and there is none.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Paragraph halka neela hona chahiye, par kuch nahi badalta. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: Class rule dot se shuru hota hai: `.note`. Uske bina CSS `<note>` tag dhoondta hai, jo hai hi nahi.

check.question: Which selector styles elements with `class="tip"`?
check.explanation: A dot means a class. `#tip` would mean an id, and `tip` would mean a `<tip>` tag.

hi.question: Kaunsa selector `class="tip"` wale elements ko style karta hai?
hi.explanation: Dot ka matlab class. `#tip` ka matlab id hota, aur `tip` ka matlab `<tip>` tag.

exercise.prompt: Give the second paragraph the class `highlight`, and make `.highlight` have a yellow `background-color`.
exercise.promptHi: Doosre paragraph ko class `highlight` do, aur `.highlight` ko peela `background-color` do.
